In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Okhotsk sea ice cover and Kamchatka glacier extent were closely coupled over the past 350 kyr, and that Kamchatka glaciers reached their maximum extents in the early and the late MIS 6 and during MIS 3, with the highest IRD accumulation rates observed during the late MIS 5.2–5.1 and MIS 4.

IRD fluxes from the eastern Okhotsks Sea reflect the presence of a persistent, but highly dynamic sea-ice cover during glacial and full glacial periods, whereas IRD fluxes and their mineralogical composition from the western Okhotks Sea are indicative of the presence and extent of the Kamchatka glaciers during MIS 6 and MIS 3.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the Okhotsk sea-ice cover was not a barrier for IRD dispersal, and that IRD records from the Okhotsk can be used for reconstructing the history of Kamchatka mountain glaciation.
